name: San Francisco
title: Holidays in San Francisco
intro: Cable cars, the Golden Gate Bridge and sea lions on the pier. Here's what San Francisco is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: September and October are the warmest, sunniest months. Summer is surprisingly cool and foggy, so pack jumpers. Winter is mild but brings most of the year's rain.

things.name: Golden Gate Bridge
things.blurb: Hire bikes and ride across to Sausalito, then take the ferry back.

things.name: Cable cars
things.blurb: Hang on as they climb the city's steep hills.

things.name: Alcatraz
things.blurb: A boat to the old island prison. Book weeks ahead.

things.name: Exploratorium
things.blurb: Hundreds of hands-on science exhibits on the waterfront.

things.name: California Academy of Sciences
things.blurb: A rainforest, aquarium and planetarium in one building.

things.name: Pier 39 sea lions
things.blurb: Hundreds of noisy sea lions lounging on the docks.

faqs.question: Is San Francisco good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's compact, full of hands-on museums, and the views are amazing. Some downtown streets are rough, so plan routes and stay in areas like Fisherman's Wharf or the Marina.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Four or five nights, often as part of a California road trip with Yosemite or the coast.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: Most British passport holders, children included, apply for an ESTA online before they fly rather than a visa. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: Can you see redwoods nearby?
faqs.answer: Yes, Muir Woods is about 40 minutes north. You need to book parking or a shuttle ahead.
